clue.text: Sea snail from Turkey into paddling

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

indicators.note: paddling splashes the water about, so the word into is stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A marine creature has been brought from Turkey and dropped into shallow water for a paddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paddling' shuffles INTO to give ITON, which follows TR.
explanation.definitionFit: The triton is a large predatory marine gastropod whose shell was used as a trumpet.

clue.text: Bird found in or near Headingley

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning the gap between two of them

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reports a sighting at or close to Headingley, the Leeds cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'neaR HEAdingley'. Headingley is a Test cricket ground in Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Posh French wine tipped over fast, making a mess

indicators.note: in a down clue, tipped over means the words before it are turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage
brut is a very dry French sparkling wine
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a bottle of fancy French wine and makes a mess of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped over' turns U BRUT round to TURBU, then LENT is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turbulent is disorderly and chaotic, causing upheaval, which fits creating a mess.

clue.text: Sea nymph: I need to swim around river

indicators.note: around tells us the jumbled letters wrap themselves about the river's letter
to swim suggests the letters of I need moving freely into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A sea nymph declares she must go swimming around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swim' shuffles INEED into NEEID, and 'around' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Nereids were the fifty sea-nymph daughters of Nereus.

clue.text: Cricketer catches hard ball at last, before England's opener can check

indicators.note: catches means the cricketer's name holds another letter within it

parts.note: Jonathan Trott is a former England batsman
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of ball
opener points to the first letter of England's

explanation.surface: A fielder takes a catch off a hard ball late on, before England's opening batsman can stop it.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Trott batted for England. 'catches' puts H inside TROTT, then come the last letter of 'ball' and the first of 'England's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle is to choke or restrict, as one checks an engine or a flow.

clue.text: He has a heavenly face

parts.note: a figure whose face is seen in the sky, made out from the markings on a celestial body at night

explanation.surface: A compliment to someone strikingly handsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly' looks like praise for good looks, but it means in the heavens: the face people see in the dark patches on the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore sees a human face in the lunar surface; that figure is the only face that is literally heavenly.

clue.text: Band-aid covered knee evenly and lasted

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band

indicators.note: covered means the band and the aid enclose the letters picked from knee

parts.note: aid taken as written, meaning help

indicators.note: evenly picks the even-placed letters, second and fourth, of knee

explanation.surface: A sticking plaster went on a grazed knee and stayed put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band-aid' splits into REM and AID. 'evenly' takes NE from 'knee', and 'covered' puts it inside AID.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay or continue, so remained means stayed on or endured.

clue.text: Giant bird, one with green tail

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
a means one

indicators.note: tail points to the final letter of green

explanation.surface: A huge bird with a green tail feather is spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were a race of giant gods in Greek myth, so a titan is any giant.

clue.text: Infatuated fool exchanges I for U following scrabble solve

indicators.note: following places the second part after the jumbled word
to scrabble is to scramble about, so the letters of solve are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of solve are the anagram fodder

indicators.note: exchanges I for U tells us one letter of the word for fool is swapped out for another

parts.note: to trick someone is to fool them

explanation.surface: A besotted player at Scrabble swaps tiles, trading an I for a U, after working out a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrabble' shuffles SOLVE into LOVES. 'exchanges I for U' turns TRICK into TRUCK, and 'following' puts it after.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lovestruck is overcome by romantic feeling, besotted with another person.

clue.text: Peter Pan, 'e carries fairy, regularly seen in orchard?

indicators.note: carries says the jumbled name holds other letters inside it
to pan is to criticise harshly or to swirl gold-bearing gravel, so the letters of Peter are knocked about
regularly picks alternate letters of fairy, here the second and fourth

parts.note: 'e is a dropped-aitch he, standing for E

explanation.surface: The boy who never grew up has a fairy with him, a regular sight in an orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Pan's fairy, Tinker Bell, makes the surface cosy, but 'Pan' shuffles PETER into PETRE. 'regularly' gives AR from 'fairy'; 'carries' puts it inside, and E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear tree is a fruit tree, one of the things grown in an orchard, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Reject the origins of theory of mind? I have a reason

indicators.note: reject means throw back, so the picked letters are read backwards
the origins of picks the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A psychologist dismisses the basics of theory of mind but insists on a rationale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the origins of' takes TOM from 'theory of mind', and 'Reject' turns it round to MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the reason or incentive that makes someone act.

clue.text: Narnia? Um, is it about Christian doctrine?

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of the four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reader wonders whether the Narnia books are really about Christian teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: C.S. Lewis's Narnia stories are famously Christian allegory, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Unitarianism is a Christian belief system rejecting the Trinity and holding that God is one person.

clue.text: Excellent channel for funky music?

parts.note: rare can mean excellent or fine, as in a rare treat
a groove is a channel or furrow

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a station is a good one to tune in for funk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' suggests a radio or TV station, but here it is a cut furrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare groove is a genre label for obscure soul and funk records sought by collectors and DJs.

clue.text: Vegetable for royal beer

parts.note: K stands for king, the royal
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A greengrocer offers to swap a vegetable for a regal brew.
explanation.definitionFit: Kale is a leafy green cabbage-family plant eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Bad weather that's most cold, right?

indicators.note: bad signals the letters that follow are spoilt and reshuffled

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is
most taken as written as anagram fodder
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A forecaster asks whether the worst weather is the coldest, isn't it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad weather' looks like the definition, but 'Bad' is the anagram signal on IE, MOST, C and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice storm is a weather event of freezing rain coating everything in a glaze.

clue.text: Merry Christmas begins with vigil, not with pudding

parts.note: merry is a slang way of saying slightly drunk, tipsy

indicators.note: begins points to the opening letter of Christmas
not means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: a wake is a vigil kept over a dead body

explanation.surface: A merry Christmas opens with a midnight watch, and no dessert follows.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the start of 'Christmas'; 'not' drops W from WAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy cake is a British trifle-like dessert of sponge soaked in sherry or wine.

clue.text: Bill overwhelmed by threat to break nail again

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the bill is swamped, sitting inside the other letters
to break means the letters of threat are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: An invoice buried under a menacing letter makes someone break a nail again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' shuffles THREAT into REATTH, and AC sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail is to fix or fasten, so to nail again is to fasten once more.

clue.text: He leaves the Beatles playing around to Hold Me Tight?

indicators.note: leaves says the letters of He are taken out of the band's name
playing around means the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Beatle quits, and the rest of the band play their song Hold Me Tight.
explanation.walkthrough: Take HE out of THE BEATLES and 'playing around' rearranges TBEATLES. 'Hold Me Tight' is a Beatles song.
explanation.definitionFit: A car or plane restraint's job is to keep you held firmly in your seat; the question mark flags the playful definition.

clue.text: Fairy king's vessel capsized

indicators.note: capsized means overturned, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king
a cup is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: The fairy king's boat has overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, which 'capsized' supports, but it is a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Puck is the mischievous sprite in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Summerhouse is roughly 83% double-glazed, polished, but not dull

indicators.note: roughly 83% means keep about five sixths of the word, the first ten of its twelve letters
but not removes the letters of dull, in order, from what is left
polished means refined or worked over, so the leftover letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden building is mostly double-glazed and gleaming rather than drab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly 83%' keeps DOUBLEGLAZ; 'but not' takes out D, U, L, L, leaving OBEGAZ, which 'polished' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open garden pavilion, the sort of summerhouse used for shade and views.

clue.text: How to get over the Beatles breaking up?

definitions.text: How to get over the Beatles breaking up?

parts.words: How to get over the Beatles breaking up?
parts.note: a band is a group, so a fan grieving its split might be treated in a counselling session

explanation.surface: A heartbroken fan wonders how to recover from the band's split.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles are a group, and the treatment for its break-up is joked to be the shared counselling session.
explanation.definitionFit: Group therapy is psychological treatment done in a meeting of several people together.

clue.text: Separate union supported by 1 in 10, maybe?

indicators.note: in a down clue supported by means the first part sits above the second
in puts the figure one inside the jumbled ten
maybe suggests another possible arrangement, so the letters of ten are reshuffled

parts.note: ten written out from the figure
the figure one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A union is split up when one member in ten gives it backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns TEN into NTE, and 'in' puts I inside it to give NTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to undo a knot, freeing or parting things that were tied together.

clue.text: Nymph born thus

parts.note: née, the French for born, gives NE in crosswords
so means thus

explanation.surface: A nymph was born in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Neso is one of the Nereids, the sea-nymphs of Greek myth, and gives its name to a moon of Neptune.

clue.text: Shakespearean character left Italy with a …

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character leaves Italy carrying something, the clue running on into the next.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the next one for the surface; each has its own wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia is the heroine of The Merchant of Venice, who disguises herself as a lawyer.

clue.text: … piece of music, emptied out those diamonds and ran!

parts.note: an opera is a dramatic musical work

indicators.note: emptied out leaves only the shell of those, its first and last letters

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Someone takes a musical score, strips out the jewels and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran' looks like fleeing, but means managed: a business is run or operated.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine or a business is to run it, so operated means ran.

clue.text: Terry manages the live charity event

parts.note: Tel is a British pet form of the name Terry

indicators.note: manages means handles or works over, so the letters of the are rearranged

parts.note: on means live, as a broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: Terry Wogan hosts the live fundraising broadcast, as he did for Children in Need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manages' shuffles THE into ETH. Terry Wogan was the long-time BBC host of the Children in Need fundraising show.
explanation.definitionFit: A telethon is a long televised broadcast that raises money for a good cause.

clue.text: Fairy king has special robe on

indicators.note: special suggests the letters of robe are specially rearranged

explanation.surface: The king of the fairies is wearing a special gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' shuffles ROBE into OBER, and ON follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream, husband of Titania.
